rationale: Static semantic expectation: the expression constructs a plain object and asks whether it is an instance of C; it does not construct C or call f. The special isinstance hook is looked up on type(C), which is the builtin type here, not on C itself, so the ordinary __instancecheck__ method defined in C's body is not invoked. Its only call to f therefore remains unreachable, and f's subprocess.run body is deferred as well. C defines no constructor, so it cannot spawn during class construction or object creation. The required preamble is import subprocess. This expected empty result follows from Python semantics, not a tripwire run.
